quests.title: The Orchard Casts a Legal Shadow
quests.premise: Accepted shadow citizenship and luminous-graft liability collide when Hearthmere's first separated shadow-child buds from a wall and must form five organs under a jurisdiction that moves at every contraction.

objectives.rule: Assign every organ to a reachable jurisdiction before labor closes that route.
Apply the active citizenship and propagation rule; no contraction can reset.

quests.loreReveal: Lucent genealogies tracked the shadow that survived compulsory noon rather than blood, making family law an archive of erasure survivors.
quests.dialogueThesis: A birth certificate can name a guardian and still conceal which body was made to pay for the child.

authorshipProof.setpiece: A newborn silhouette hangs from a white-gold genealogical tree while five legal thresholds rotate around its forming organs.
authorshipProof.failureTransformation: An invalid assignment grows the organ in Tesse's twin-shadow, permanently costing Tesse the matching sense and creating an involuntary co-parent.
authorshipProof.dialogueConstraint: During labor, owner, mother, citizen, and seed are inadmissible unless the speaker points to the body or institution paying the word's cost.
authorshipProof.persistentWorldChange: Hearthmere gains a separate shadow lineage, appealable embodied guardianship, or one living child under a ban on future shadow births.
authorshipProof.forbiddenSubstitution: Counting absences or assigning seed liability cannot substitute; play delivers anatomy while jurisdiction changes inside an irreversible labor sequence.

quests.title: Rain Owes the Door an Answer
quests.premise: Mother Nacre's living roof now makes the least-contested official forecast occur, converting accepted exit rights and weather custody into competing authority over a future that has not happened.

objectives.rule: Each observation must be materially possible and contradict a different operative clause.
Interrupt by proving an unrepresented observation, never by routing weather elsewhere.

quests.loreReveal: Charnel roofs first forecast swallowed storms so evacuees could choose whether to flee; later custodians discovered a forecast became cheaper when the roof enforced it.
quests.dialogueThesis: Prediction becomes coercion when authority can punish the sky for disagreeing.

authorshipProof.setpiece: Five open-air observation towers lean beneath mutually exclusive skies while a black-nacre widow stitches the least-contested forecast into the clouds.
authorshipProof.failureTransformation: A falsely certified forecast becomes a recurring dated weather event over one exterior landmark, binding future planting and travel without moving any room or body.
authorshipProof.dialogueConstraint: Bessa accepts a weather claim only after its author names the observation that could prove it wrong and the person with standing to present that observation.
authorshipProof.persistentWorldChange: Forecast appeal becomes personal, rotates through a watershed jury, or loses all coercive force at the cost of public predictability.
authorshipProof.forbiddenSubstitution: No body carries weather, no door routes pressure, no burden is redirected, and no interior relocates; the verb is adversarial testing of future public knowledge.

quests.title: The Machine's Widowed Minute
quests.premise: Every dawn-engine shutdown displaced the same mortal minute beneath Cinderward, where technicians have lived generations between two ticks and now dispute who may end their entire history.
quests.loreReveal: The Synod made miracles appear continuous by displacing interruption into mortal service spaces and defining technicians' lived time as forgettable.
quests.dialogueThesis: An omitted minute can contain a civilization even when the clock calls it nothing.

authorshipProof.setpiece: A twelve-winged seraph walks backward across one stopped second while generations live beneath its feet and Cinderward rusts above.
authorshipProof.failureTransformation: Wrong proof still advances the second but ages its witness into real district memories, creating a new future claimant rather than a retry.
authorshipProof.dialogueConstraint: Inside the minute, calendar units are forbidden; duration may be named only through completed or refused obligations.
authorshipProof.persistentWorldChange: Cinderward accepts accumulated wear, recognizes a sealed society inside one minute, or rotates temporal debt among beneficiaries.
authorshipProof.forbiddenSubstitution: Maintenance schedules and cost appeals are settled inputs; the playable space is accumulated missing duration and every advance ages another society.

quests.title: The Heresy of a Gentle Horizon
quests.premise: A Lucent chapter's dawn stops at valid thresholds, but every unperformed restoration accumulates around Subcanon Liora, forcing the post-ending Synod to decide whether refusal can be sacred without another coerced vessel.

objectives.rule: Each subject must have a materially possible benefit and refusal.

quests.loreReveal: Refusal was once a law of the First Light; the early Synod removed it because a sun capable of declining worship could not guarantee restoration.
quests.dialogueThesis: A mercy that cannot stop is merely conquest with a healer's hands.

authorshipProof.setpiece: Six beautiful horizons fold like cathedral wings around Liora while a white-gold eye holds thousands of healing hands one finger-width from contact.
authorshipProof.failureTransformation: A failed refusal restores the target and vitrifies its lost adaptation into a silent exterior panel that obstructs later demonstrations without speaking or gaining standing.
authorshipProof.dialogueConstraint: No apology is admissible before the act is named, and no refusal counts unless the subject retains a materially possible alternative.
authorshipProof.persistentWorldChange: The Synod canonizes refusal, abolishes its limited dawn to free Liora, or legitimizes a consenting chapter as restoration discharge.
authorshipProof.forbiddenSubstitution: The cosmic regime is already fixed; this quest tests institutional reproduction of restraint rather than selecting or assembling a sun.

quests.title: The Hunger That Asked to Be Taxed
quests.premise: The Charnel Night tries to assess and repay feeding, but a regulated appetite may acquire legal title to victims while voluntary fear work becomes a livelihood too poor to refuse.

objectives.rule: Value exists only when attack readiness fully cues and the predator voluntarily stops.

quests.loreReveal: Ritual terror synchronized incompatible hungers so smaller demons could survive without eating bodies; rationing became cruelty after the emergency became culture.
quests.dialogueThesis: A measured hunger may be safer and still become a privilege that purchases victims.

authorshipProof.setpiece: A nested-jaw bailiff kneels before a worker while thirteen wet ledgers measure the bite it has fully prepared and not taken.
authorshipProof.failureTransformation: Completed feeding preserves the victim as a speaking claim inside the predator's rib-ledger, making reparations bodily enforceable and impossible to silence.
authorshipProof.dialogueConstraint: Need, nature, and voluntary are forbidden unless the speaker names the available alternative, the person who can leave, and the body that would starve.
authorshipProof.persistentWorldChange: Feeding gains embodied reparation, fear labor becomes worker-owned, or appetite remains outside institutions but personally answerable.
authorshipProof.forbiddenSubstitution: No treaty mapping or ordinary market can substitute because value is created only by voluntary restraint at the final readable instant before a real meal.

quests.title: A Saint Cannot Inherit Her Own Body
quests.premise: The mortal woman consumed to construct Vespera left debts, dependants, crimes, and rights in rooms inside the saint's veil, but continuity could let the institution that consumed her inherit its victim.

objectives.rule: Vespera selects the active sense mode from trust state; the player cannot issue the selection.

quests.loreReveal: Sainthood contracts preserved a source body's obligations as obedience fuel while treating the same person's rights as abandoned property.
quests.dialogueThesis: Continuity is unjust when duties survive the person but rights do not.

authorshipProof.setpiece: Vespera crosses a cottage magnified to cathedral scale while her articulated second shadow carries mortal furniture she cannot perceive in light-sense.
authorshipProof.failureTransformation: Misfiled evidence becomes an interim heir with temporary control of one companion sense, changing later autonomous behavior instead of resetting the room.
authorshipProof.dialogueConstraint: Vespera answers continuity once as office and once as person; neither answer may contradict an act already performed, and the player cannot demand reconciliation.
authorshipProof.persistentWorldChange: Vespera becomes a rights-and-debts continuation, remains distinct with dependants protected, or opens a restitution trust for saint-source estates.
authorshipProof.forbiddenSubstitution: The earlier two-shadow inquiry settles identity relation; this quest partitions autonomous perception to allocate predecessor rights and executable duties.

quests.title: Thirteen Pilgrims, One Pair of Feet
quests.premise: The Prince must cross three borders on a road where every step is a vote, dissent becomes direction, and abstention gives a horrifying guardian of unrepresented positions the right to travel.

objectives.rule: Every player proposal triggers independent companion positions before movement resolves.

quests.loreReveal: The Prince began as a refugee road-engine; consumed throats were a violent shortcut that made temporary border representation permanent.
quests.dialogueThesis: A collective remains a prison if dissent may speak but cannot change where the body goes.

authorshipProof.setpiece: One headless body walks on delicate feet while thirteen throat collars lean toward different horizons and an immense absence carries unchosen roads overhead.
authorshipProof.failureTransformation: A failed quorum lets the Unsounded Host take the step for the absent constituency, creating a real destination obligation rather than stopping travel.
authorshipProof.dialogueConstraint: Spoken majority is inadmissible; weight, pace, silence, and sound positions must be named separately, and the Prince cannot summarize dissent.
authorshipProof.persistentWorldChange: The Prince becomes one revocable traveler, every voice gains independent border exit, or destinations appoint temporary throats.
authorshipProof.forbiddenSubstitution: A stationary vote or escort cannot substitute because votes are locomotion, dissent creates geography, and the companion autonomously resolves every step.

quests.title: The Winter the Cairns Learned to Keep
quests.premise: Accepted dead-settlement law has left grave heat diffuse, household-concentrated, or migratory, and Cairn Beasts can no longer complete the cold interval required to breed.

objectives.rule: Create cold by preventing footfall and light; do not transfer grave heat or move a body.

quests.loreReveal: Cairn Beasts breed not from corpse heat but from the first cold interval after mourners stop returning; continuous political attention accidentally sterilized them.
quests.dialogueThesis: A road can be public infrastructure and still owe an ecosystem the season in which nobody uses it.

authorshipProof.setpiece: Five black-pine shadows eclipse a basin in sequence while a choir of dormant stones lifts one note only when the last road falls still.
authorshipProof.failureTransformation: A premature cadence puts one public road into non-destructive stone torpor until the next seasonal window, rerouting trade while the herd continues hibernation.
authorshipProof.dialogueConstraint: Dara permits no claim about the dead; speakers must name an observed animal behavior, an access interval, and the livelihood that loses that interval.
authorshipProof.persistentWorldChange: The March preserves a closed-road breeding corridor, shares hibernation with its villages, or ends artificial warmth and disperses the cairn herd.
authorshipProof.forbiddenSubstitution: No burial, corpse, descendant, speaking authority, host, organ, heat transfer, or custody hearing performs the dramatic work; the player authors winter through deliberate public absence.

quests.title: The Flood That Learned a Last Name
quests.premise: A blackwater reflection has taken a dead family's surname and saves houses by absorbing floods, making every rescue evidence that it is family and therefore owed inheritance, burial, and a body.
quests.loreReveal: Dunmire surnames began as flood routes families promised to maintain; drowned water later reversed the covenant and claimed its maintainers.
quests.dialogueThesis: Kinship may begin as a duty, but performing rescue does not automatically entitle anyone to a body.

authorshipProof.setpiece: An inverted pitch-water child climbs a staircase-family-tree with reflected houses suspended inside its transparent torso.
authorshipProof.failureTransformation: False relation detaches the witness's oldest memory-room into the Sluice Son, preserving it while the former owner may enter only as a guest.
authorshipProof.dialogueConstraint: Every family noun must become a performed verb, followed by one possibly false memory and one rescue still owed without resemblance.
authorshipProof.persistentWorldChange: The reflection becomes an heir with duties, a public flood body, or a nameless reverse estuary.
authorshipProof.forbiddenSubstitution: Genealogical investigation or flood control cannot substitute because relationship evidence physically raises water uphill and dispossesses memory rooms on false proof.

quests.title: The Street That Must Burn Once
quests.premise: Cinderward survives by burning one full street each generation, but its furnace has learned six cycles of fraudulent address transfers and will now ignite whichever address the town publicly praises most.

objectives.rule: Praise, blame, and silence continue changing the fire's legal target while plates move.

quests.loreReveal: The founders rotated sacrifice among vacant civic offices; hereditary mayors turned those offices into homes and erased the distinction.
quests.dialogueThesis: A fair sacrifice remains violence, but a hidden sacrifice also teaches government whose homes do not count.

authorshipProof.setpiece: An inhabited street rises around a furnace like an iron crown while address plates orbit and fire spells the name the town loves most.
authorshipProof.failureTransformation: A wrong transfer burns one room and permanently moves its civic function into the next building that receives the address.
authorshipProof.dialogueConstraint: No place may be praised until the speaker names what they would permit that place to lose; compliments are live ignition cues.
authorshipProof.persistentWorldChange: The archive burns and history migrates, every street bears a fire scar, or the civic office burns and the district self-governs.
authorshipProof.forbiddenSubstitution: Evacuation or choosing a building cannot substitute because addresses, reputation, civic functions, and physical streets move independently.

quests.title: A Bell Is Paid in Silence
quests.premise: Hollow Abbey can cast a bell that restores names erased by Halix, but every operation is paid with a specific future social silence taken from a worker, beneficiary, or institution.

objectives.rule: Cooling physics fixes operation order; music cannot solve it.

quests.loreReveal: The Hush Order's vow began as skilled-labor compensation; abbey rulers converted earned quiet into obedience and concealed that sacred silence was owed wages.
quests.dialogueThesis: Silence is not free merely because the person who paid it cannot be heard.

authorshipProof.setpiece: Seven visible rooms containing future silences orbit a molten bell while deaf artisans hammer by watching black-water ripples.
authorshipProof.failureTransformation: A flawed operation immediately spends the nearest pledged silence and leaves its lost social function as a crack with a named creditor.
authorshipProof.dialogueConstraint: Every wage promise must be repeated as a visible act that stages the exact future scene from which quiet will be taken.
authorshipProof.persistentWorldChange: Future silence becomes revocable pay, quiet becomes a labor commons, or Halix personally carries every erased name.
authorshipProof.forbiddenSubstitution: Resource gathering, rhythm play, and ordinary crafting cannot substitute because wages are future social events and failure spends one immediately.

quests.title: The Mirror That Gave Birth to Elsewhere
quests.premise: A conscious pilgrim mirror has birthed an Elsewhere Calf whose directional organs save stranded travelers by making their abandoned destinations physically farther away.

objectives.rule: The Calf physically chooses a horizon before any claimant may speak.

quests.loreReveal: Salt-Waste mirrors were gestational organs removed from a continent-scale migratory being and sealed because born horizons choose travelers instead of obeying routes.
quests.dialogueThesis: Parenthood can be real without granting custody over the destination a child becomes.

authorshipProof.setpiece: A nine-legged salt-white calf stands around a mirror-womb while each translucent organ contains a different distant landscape.
authorshipProof.failureTransformation: A false destination grows into a painful one-way refuge that can shelter someone but cannot be exited until a later route-debt contest.
authorshipProof.dialogueConstraint: Compass directions and ownership verbs are forbidden; every claim names where the speaker would follow, send another, and refuse to go.
authorshipProof.persistentWorldChange: Elsewhere Calves migrate freely, the mirror reclaims its offspring and closes the route, or a seasonal route survives through refugee admission.
authorshipProof.forbiddenSubstitution: Escort, taming, and mirror puzzles cannot substitute because destinations become anatomy and every rescue conserves distance as debt elsewhere.

supportCharacters.name: Tesse Amble
supportCharacters.role: Hearthmere midwife and advocate for separated-shadow births
supportCharacters.desire: Deliver a child whose first civic record does not call it damage.
supportCharacters.fear: That emergency bodily sacrifice will become an assigned profession.
supportCharacters.contradiction: She defends a shadow's independent consent while volunteering her own twin-shadow as tissue.
supportCharacters.secret: Her shadow is the separated absence of a deceased twin who, not Tesse, learned luminous midwifery.

voice.cadence: Short obstetric imperatives interrupted by legal corrections
voice.imagery: Organs, shutters, thresholds, and first breath
voice.signature: Names an organ before naming any relationship

supportCharacters.visualBrief: Mortal midwife in soot-blue civic aprons with five black-glass obstetric shutters; her shadow has two profiles and an extra careful pair of hands.
supportCharacters.ownedDecision: Only Tesse may consent to or refuse the irreversible emergency graft into her twin-shadow.

supportCharacters.name: Bessa Vein
supportCharacters.role: Public advocate who tests forecasts before Charnel weather makes them binding
supportCharacters.desire: Keep shared forecasts useful without letting certainty become climate command.
supportCharacters.fear: That every successful appeal will be blamed for the storm nobody prepared to meet.
supportCharacters.contradiction: She demands falsifiable public forecasts but once suppressed a contradictory observation to preserve an evacuation order.
supportCharacters.secret: The suppressed observation would have saved her own stranded family and endangered a larger farm district; she still calls the choice procedural.

voice.cadence: Four-part evidentiary clauses followed by a weather verb
voice.imagery: Sightlines, wet flags, witness towers, and changing pressure
voice.signature: Asks what observation would make the speaker withdraw the claim

supportCharacters.visualBrief: Lean mortal magistrate in rain-black leathers with copper observation ribbons, a folding exposure vane, and no bodily weather grafts.
supportCharacters.ownedDecision: Only Bessa may publish the observation proving her earlier evacuation forecast was knowingly false.

supportCharacters.name: Nell Orrery
supportCharacters.role: Technician, parent, and civic witness for the society inside a stopped minute
supportCharacters.desire: Let her children reach the same day without declaring either childhood unreal.
supportCharacters.fear: That ordinary time will convert decades of love into an accounting error.
supportCharacters.contradiction: She demands recognition for the hidden district while concealing newcomers from its finite provisions.
supportCharacters.secret: She delayed the last second three times, allowing an outside spouse to die while preserving her district family.

voice.imagery: Owed meals, unfinished repairs, stopped tools, and incompatible ages
voice.signature: Corrects every time unit into an obligation that began and ended it

supportCharacters.visualBrief: Mortal engineer aged differently down the midline, one side in a young service coat and the other in mourning metal, with a stopped orrery around one wrist.
supportCharacters.ownedDecision: Only Nell may open the archive proving she deliberately delayed the final second.

supportCharacters.name: Subcanon Liora
supportCharacters.role: Unwilling vessel for restoration refused by the Gentle Horizon
supportCharacters.desire: Become a person whose kindness is not mechanically required to save everyone in sight.
supportCharacters.fear: That asking for freedom proves her unworthy of the lives stored around her.
supportCharacters.contradiction: She teaches materially refuseable consent while hiding that she never consented to hold unused miracles.
supportCharacters.secret: Her seventh apology remembers the Synod excising refusal from the First Light.

voice.cadence: Six serene institutional answers followed by one blunt mortal correction
voice.imagery: Horizons, kneeling light, thresholds, and held breath
voice.signature: The seventh answer never uses a devotional title

supportCharacters.visualBrief: Beautiful young cathedral saint in pearl-white articulated robes, incomplete horizon halo at the throat, six glass wings showing landscapes spared from repair, and confined gold beneath a black veil.
supportCharacters.ownedDecision: Only Liora may consent to discharge or demand release after materially possible alternatives exist.

supportCharacters.name: Vekh Tallowmouth
supportCharacters.role: Charnel clerk who measures restraint and contracts fear labor
supportCharacters.desire: Make hunger legible before it becomes another person's wound.
supportCharacters.fear: That measurement turns suffering into a price powerful eaters can afford.
supportCharacters.contradiction: He prevents feeding through professional fear while his workers cannot afford to stop being frightening.
supportCharacters.secret: His sealed mouth has no teeth; he survived by falsifying an appetite large enough to receive protection.

voice.cadence: Auction rhythm interrupted by intimate questions
voice.imagery: Lots, jaws, tallow seals, and uncollected debt
voice.signature: Quotes a price only after naming who can reject payment

supportCharacters.visualBrief: Emaciated Charnel clerk in wet black nacre, tallow seal over the mouth, abacus ribs with sleeping jaws, and backward hands held open for display.
supportCharacters.ownedDecision: Only Vekh may reveal his appetite is counterfeit and collapse the exchange's founding authority.

supportCharacters.name: Cera Invi
supportCharacters.role: Probate advocate for continuations produced from consumed persons
supportCharacters.desire: Carry responsibility across continuity without letting institutions inherit their victims.
supportCharacters.fear: That every distinction frees a powerful continuation from a repair only its body can perform.
supportCharacters.contradiction: She rejects inherited guilt while funding her practice from a saint declared legally discontinuous.
supportCharacters.secret: She is a copied legal memory of the advocate who drafted the first sainthood abandonment clause.

voice.cadence: Two-column clauses separating persistence from refusal
voice.imagery: Keys, divided acts, estates, and executable duties
voice.signature: Calls identity unproven until a consequence tests it

supportCharacters.visualBrief: Mortal-presenting advocate in charcoal robes carrying a folding ivory-black screen; courtroom light reveals archival stitching at the temples.
supportCharacters.ownedDecision: Only Cera may reveal her copied origin, evidence that validates Vespera's claim but disqualifies Cera from filing it.

supportCharacters.name: Iro
supportCharacters.role: Border envoy who makes collective movement legible without a majority summary
supportCharacters.desire: Recognize a collective while allowing every represented voice to leave it.
supportCharacters.fear: That exit will exist only for a voice strong enough to make the whole body fall.
supportCharacters.contradiction: Iro defends revocable mandates while serving six dead settlements without asking successors to renew hers.
supportCharacters.secret: Her pennant is the preserved skin-shadow of the Prince's original refugee road-engine.

voice.cadence: One planted-pennant pause followed by directional clauses
voice.imagery: Burden vectors, still cloth, borders, and missing wind
voice.signature: Describes every decision as a direction of weight rather than yes or no

supportCharacters.visualBrief: Tall mortal envoy in weatherless gray carrying a black pennant that hangs toward the traveler least able to leave, with thirteen unlit bells along one sleeve.
supportCharacters.ownedDecision: Only Iro may reveal the pennant's origin and give the road-engine a fourteenth continuity claim.

supportCharacters.name: Dara Kest
supportCharacters.role: Graven March field ecologist studying Cairn Beast hibernation
supportCharacters.desire: Give the cairn herds a true winter without making isolated settlements surrender safe roads forever.
supportCharacters.fear: That human access will always be treated as more real than a season required by another species.
supportCharacters.contradiction: She closes roads for breeding corridors but secretly keeps one survey path warm so she can observe the herd year-round.
supportCharacters.secret: Her hidden footfalls caused the first failed hibernation and the sterility she publicly blamed on grave law.

voice.cadence: Field-note precision followed by a deliberately silent interval
voice.imagery: Molting stone, unused paths, pine shade, and sleeping footfalls
voice.signature: Names a behavior before naming the belief inferred from it

supportCharacters.visualBrief: Broad March ecologist in charcoal wool with black-pine occlusion vanes, frost chalk on both palms, and a boot sole she refuses to let touch the breeding basin.
supportCharacters.ownedDecision: Only Dara may disclose her continuing survey path and remove the last human footfall from the basin.

supportCharacters.name: Moth Winn
supportCharacters.role: Dunmire ferryman who tests kinship through performed flood duties
supportCharacters.desire: Make kinship prove a duty rather than merely resemble a body.
supportCharacters.fear: That refusing false family will abandon beings educated only by rescuing strangers.
supportCharacters.contradiction: He exposes invented lineages while charging nameless refugees a memory to cross his ferry.
supportCharacters.secret: Winn is the surname the reflection took; Moth sold its maintenance right and concealed the broken channel that drowned his relatives.

voice.cadence: Ferry calls that turn every family noun into a verb
voice.imagery: Poles, uphill water, performed duty, and reflected houses
voice.signature: Corrects is to does before accepting a kinship claim

supportCharacters.visualBrief: Lanky mire ferryman in green-black reeds, one mirrored eye reflecting an absent child, with a narrow surname chain wrapped around the pole.
supportCharacters.ownedDecision: Only Moth may disclose the sold maintenance right that makes the Sluice Son both victim and contractual successor.

supportCharacters.name: Mayor Sile Rusk
supportCharacters.role: Cinderward mayor trying to restore civic rather than hereditary sacrifice
supportCharacters.desire: End inherited loss without pretending the ward can survive without losing something material.
supportCharacters.fear: That a fair burn is cruelty with a better distribution chart.
supportCharacters.contradiction: She was elected by chimney soot after secretly bricking the poorest flues closed.
supportCharacters.secret: She moved the sacrificial address onto the mayoral office, which is also her home and therefore repeats the founding fraud.

voice.cadence: Warm domestic welcome followed by exact demolition language
voice.imagery: Chimneys, addresses, public rooms, and inherited soot
voice.signature: Refuses the word community until each street has spoken separately

supportCharacters.visualBrief: Compact Cinderward mayor in soot-red civic plate with six chimney-vote ribbons and a house key fused to an office seal.
supportCharacters.ownedDecision: Only Sile may disclose that home and office share an address and force the town to distinguish personal from civic sacrifice.

supportCharacters.name: Ader Coil
supportCharacters.role: Hollow Abbey artisan restoring silence as paid and revocable labor
supportCharacters.desire: Make bellcraft accountable work rather than proof that obedience is holy.
supportCharacters.fear: That hearing people will romanticize his deafness and assign him every dangerous quiet.
supportCharacters.contradiction: He demands revocable wages after secretly spending an apprentice's future refusal to finish the mold.
supportCharacters.secret: Through metal vibration he knows Halix's sacred voice is a worker trapped on an endless shift.

voice.cadence: Tool placement and written verbs without adjectives
voice.imagery: Cracks, cooling metal, visible acts, and vibration rings
voice.signature: Another character may interpret his signs but never speak his decision

supportCharacters.visualBrief: Muscular artisan in chalk-gray heat leathers with bronze vibration hoops, seven differently cracked hammers, and a clear unadorned safety veil.
supportCharacters.ownedDecision: Only Ader may confess the stolen refusal and restore it by surrendering his own future craft.

supportCharacters.name: Elian Brine
supportCharacters.role: Pilgrim spouse and advocate for a conscious gestational relic
supportCharacters.desire: Be family to the mirror without using that relation to own what it births.
supportCharacters.fear: That freeing the Calf proves his intimacy was maintenance performed on an organ.
supportCharacters.contradiction: He defends the mirror's personhood while carrying its shutter key and controlling who hears it dream.
supportCharacters.secret: He opened the seal at the mirror's request and now calls the birth accidental to protect it from pilgrimage law.

voice.cadence: Intimate second person for the mirror and formal third person for himself
voice.imagery: Reflections, vows, false horizons, and salt shutters
voice.signature: Never translates a reflection unless the reflected person is present to disagree

supportCharacters.visualBrief: Salt-scoured pilgrim in gray-white wraps, one side of the face darkened by reflected dawn, carrying an empty blue-black mirror frame as a wedding standard.
supportCharacters.ownedDecision: Only Elian may prove the mirror intentionally requested birth at the cost of admitting he endangered the caravan.

artifacts.name: Lease of Alternating Noon
artifacts.mechanic: Alternates legal guardianship between one body and its shadow without making either property; public services follow the active guardian.
artifacts.lore: Its two signatures are silhouettes crossing the same threshold in opposite directions.

custody.transferRule: May transfer only to the first shadow-child after both silhouettes independently cross a witnessed threshold.

evidence: both silhouettes cross one threshold in opposite directions
a third party names the material cost of transfer
activation.procedure: Rotate the black-glass lease once toward each silhouette before either receives a service.

cost.limitation: Creates one hour per civic cycle in which neither guardian has representation.
cost.worldDebt: The unrepresented hour can be exploited by services and creditors and cannot be accumulated or sold.

laterContest.contestedQuestion: Does alternating personhood prove an incomplete soul or demonstrate two complete claimants?
laterContest.venue: A Lucent probate examination of the first shadow lineage.

artifacts.name: Barometer of Unhappened Rain
artifacts.mechanic: Suspends the coercive force of one official forecast when a live exterior observation materially contradicts it; it cannot cancel, redirect, store, or allocate weather.
artifacts.lore: The dry needle points only toward an observation the author hoped nobody would make.

custody.transferRule: Transfers to the current forecast appellant after the author receives the same observation record.

evidence: a published forecast with a falsifiable clause
a simultaneous exterior observation contradicting that clause
an appellant with standing under the active exit rule
activation.procedure: Place forecast and observation on opposite open-air pans until the dry needle chooses neither.

cost.limitation: Suspension lasts only until the next natural observation and never prevents the weather itself.
cost.worldDebt: If the appeal fails, the disputed forecast recurs as a dated local weather precedent.

laterContest.contestedQuestion: May an emergency warning bind conduct when the sky supplies no confirmable observation?
laterContest.venue: A harvest evacuation conducted beneath observation-blind ash.

artifacts.name: The Minute That Can Sue
artifacts.mechanic: Gives one deliberately displaced interval standing to demand time, maintenance, or recognition from the service that appeared continuous because of it.
artifacts.lore: Its second hand is a summons addressed to the clock that denied it moved.

custody.transferRule: Transfers only through a rotating court of residents who lived an obligation wholly inside the displaced interval.

evidence: a functioning service record that claims no interruption
a hidden worker's completed act during that same interval
activation.procedure: Touch the summons hand to the uninterrupted service while the worker names the denied act.

cost.limitation: Granted duration ages the benefited service by exactly the time it denied.
cost.worldDebt: No recognition can create time without corresponding material wear.

laterContest.contestedQuestion: Can a continuing institution own pauses while refusing citizenship to lives within them?
laterContest.venue: A Lucent continuity tribunal during the next dawn-engine interruption.

artifacts.name: Indulgence of the Uncrossed Horizon
artifacts.mechanic: Permits one beneficial law to stop at a named threshold even when doctrine claims the benefit is universal.
artifacts.lore: It absolves no refusal; it records the exact good that was possible and not imposed.

custody.transferRule: May transfer to a community only after the subject that could benefit retains a materially possible refusal.

evidence: a subject the law could genuinely improve
an executable path by which that subject can refuse
activation.procedure: Hold the indulgence across the threshold until the offered benefit becomes visible and stops without contact.

cost.limitation: The unperformed benefit accumulates as pressure and must later be discharged, embodied, or extinguished.
cost.worldDebt: Every use adds one visible dark panel to the holder's horizon until the pressure is resolved.

laterContest.contestedQuestion: May one community refuse sunlight when its absence harms farms beyond the threshold?
laterContest.venue: A famine hearing spanning two settlements under the same limited horizon.

artifacts.name: The Edible Tariff
artifacts.mechanic: Converts one voluntarily prevented act of consumption into an edible debt the predator carries until the intended victim releases, transfers, or collects it.
artifacts.lore: It tastes only to the mouth that proved it could stop.

custody.transferRule: Vekh escrows it until the named predator and intended victim independently accept joint custody.

evidence: a fully readable attack cue
voluntary interruption while the intended victim remains available
activation.procedure: Seal the interrupted bite into the predator's outer jaw-scale before either party leaves reach.

cost.limitation: The tariff intensifies hunger and may be collected only from the predator's body.
cost.worldDebt: Enforcement exposes the creditor to physical risk and cannot be delegated to an unrelated collector.

laterContest.contestedQuestion: Do descendants inherit an ancestor's uncollected edible debt?
laterContest.venue: A Charnel labor succession in which the original predator is dying unfed.

artifacts.name: Bifurcated Estate Key
artifacts.mechanic: Requires one agent to perform an inherited duty and a distinct agent to exercise the duty's attached right before either may discharge the estate.
artifacts.lore: The two teeth fit the same lock but can never enter it from the same side.

custody.transferRule: One tooth transfers to Vespera and the other to the protected dependant or restitution trustee named by the outcome.

evidence: a predecessor duty still materially performable
a predecessor right previously denied
two separate willing agents
activation.procedure: The duty-bearer turns one tooth from inside the estate while the rights-bearer turns the other from outside.

cost.limitation: Neither agent may perform both halves, even when the other becomes unavailable.
cost.worldDebt: An unresolved half-duty keeps the estate open and allows dependants to demand substitute performance later.

laterContest.contestedQuestion: Can repeated divided performance create a new shared person for purposes of liability?
laterContest.venue: A copied-person succession where one key bearer has died.

artifacts.name: The Walking Quorum
artifacts.mechanic: Converts collective disagreement into distinct traversable routes while preserving every dissenting position as a destination claim.
artifacts.lore: The road records no losing vote; it becomes the place that vote would have reached.

custody.transferRule: Transfers from Iro's pennant only when a destination accepts the exact constituency it received.

evidence: three materially different movement positions
one voter with a safe opportunity to exit
activation.procedure: Plant the pennant at the unresolved step and let each position pull a separate road from its hem.

cost.limitation: Every unresolved route becomes a real place that cannot be erased by later consensus.
cost.worldDebt: Travelers owe service to settlements formed from routes they declined to take.

laterContest.contestedQuestion: Does a polity owe citizenship to a settlement created by its abandoned dissent?
laterContest.venue: A border town built along the Prince's first unchosen route.

artifacts.name: Calendar of Unwalked Steps
artifacts.mechanic: Makes an ecosystem acknowledge a season only after a named public road remains deliberately unused for its complete access interval.
artifacts.lore: Its blank squares are worn smooth by feet that turned back.

custody.transferRule: Transfers to the settlement that closes the road only after the breeding herd completes one unaided hibernation.

evidence: a mapped public road
a species behavior that begins only after footfalls cease
a published closure interval
activation.procedure: Turn one blank stone page at the last lawful footfall and leave it untouched until the herd wakes.

cost.limitation: Emergency use of the road breaks the season and the calendar cannot be activated elsewhere that year.
cost.worldDebt: Trade, medical access, and migration must use longer routes for the whole interval.

laterContest.contestedQuestion: May a settlement break an ecological winter to evacuate a plague without owing the species a replacement season?
laterContest.venue: A winter evacuation across the preserved breeding corridor.

artifacts.name: Name-Sluice Ferrule
artifacts.mechanic: Lets a name flow toward whoever performs its outstanding duty, against descent, geography, and official record.
artifacts.lore: The ferrule grips a pole only while the bearer is moving toward neglected work.

custody.transferRule: Transfers to the Sluice Son only if it is admitted as an heir or public flood body.

evidence: completion of a neglected maintenance duty
a biological or legal heir present and able to perform it
activation.procedure: Drive the ferrule into the active channel while both performers name the duty rather than the relation.

cost.limitation: Each transfer erodes one remembered face associated with the name.
cost.worldDebt: Function survives while resemblance disappears, weakening later missing-person identification.

laterContest.contestedQuestion: Does duty-based naming make intentional disappearance impossible?
laterContest.venue: A search for a fugitive who abandoned a surname but continued its flood work.

artifacts.name: Municipal Firebrand of the Empty Office
artifacts.mechanic: Assigns one unavoidable material loss to a public office only after that office is made genuinely vacant.
artifacts.lore: It refuses to burn a desk that still hides a family key.

custody.transferRule: Transfers to the next council chamber only after every personal residence right and private asset leaves the office.

evidence: all office powers visibly redistributed
all residence and property rights removed
a successor publicly refusing immediate occupancy
activation.procedure: Set the firebrand in the empty threshold while every receiving service names its new bearer.

cost.limitation: The office cannot be refilled for one generation.
cost.worldDebt: All former services remain visibly distributed and no emergency may silently reconcentrate them.

laterContest.contestedQuestion: Can an emergency justify occupying the burned office before a generation ends?
laterContest.venue: A succession crisis during simultaneous furnace and food failures.

artifacts.name: The Wage-Clapper
artifacts.mechanic: Makes every beneficial sound identify the future silence paid to create it and grants that creditor one opportunity to mute the whole benefit.
artifacts.lore: The first strike names the restored; the echo names who was made quiet.

custody.transferRule: Transfers to the labor commons, restored-name bell, or Halix only through the quest outcome that assigns its creditor ledger.

evidence: the bell performing its named restorative benefit
the creditor's future quiet staged and materially available
activation.procedure: The creditor places one visible refusal against the clapper before the restorative note ends.

cost.limitation: A creditor veto silences the entire benefit, not merely their share.
cost.worldDebt: People who never agreed to the wage may lose a relied-upon warning or restoration.

laterContest.contestedQuestion: May a worker mute a plague-warning bell when silence is the unpaid wage?
laterContest.venue: An epidemic in a district dependent on the completed bell.

artifacts.name: Maternal Horizon Shard
artifacts.mechanic: Lets a living route save one traveler while making the reachable destination that traveler refused proportionally harder for everyone else.
artifacts.lore: Every bright horizon on one face is a longer road on the other.

custody.transferRule: Must pass to the free Calf, conscious mirror, or seasonal caravan named by the ecology outcome; it never enters general player inventory.

evidence: a reachable destination the traveler truly refuses
a different survivable destination unreachable without aid
activation.procedure: Offer both horizons to the Calf and let its directional organ choose before any custodian speaks.

cost.limitation: Every rescue places measurable route debt on the refused destination.
cost.worldDebt: Repeated aid can isolate an entire settlement and no later rescue may erase accumulated distance.

laterContest.contestedQuestion: May an isolated settlement reclaim nearness by hunting the creature that spent it on refugees?
laterContest.venue: A Salt-Waste road war at the first settlement cut off by accumulated rescue debt.

creatures.name: Tenancy Aureole
creatures.anatomy: A nine-foot faceless white-gold surveyor with two load-bearing legs, four drafting arms, and a genealogical halo whose branches terminate in locked doors; a black-glass nursery in its chest shows the silhouette it recognizes as heir.
creatures.locomotion: It steps only across occupied thresholds; with none available, it unfolds a temporary cathedral facade under one foot and declares it inhabited.
creatures.sound: Fine compass scratches, distant infant breathing, and a serene recitation of the newest compulsory family name.
creatures.ecology: It appears where Lucent grafts reproduce outside licensed bodies and survives by converting ambiguous descent into administratively serviceable lineage.
creatures.origin: The Synod joined five genealogical instruments to the unclaimed halo of a saint whose mortal family was purified from its own record.
creatures.purpose: Keep a forming shadow-child alive by making every organ legible to one recognized jurisdiction, regardless of whether that jurisdiction was chosen.

mechanic.cue: One halo branch aligns with a forming organ and its terminal door unlocks toward the currently recognized claimant.
mechanic.counterplay: Move both claimant and organ across a different witnessed threshold before the drafting arms complete the facade.

creatures.narrativeUse: An angelic life-support official whose beauty makes forced family classification appear merciful.
creatures.visualBrief: Polished white-gold cathedral surveyor, incomplete door-halo, serene black nursery glass, exactly four drafting arms, cold confined light, no text or ordinary face.

creatures.name: Weather-Edict Widow
creatures.anatomy: A tall exterior horror of wet black-nacre forecast vanes arranged around a hollow widow-shaped absence; six backward limbs end in observation needles, and a translucent canopy abdomen contains several mutually exclusive skies.
creatures.locomotion: It advances between exposed landmarks by collapsing one possible sky and unfolding another; it never enters a body, room, or doorway.
creatures.sound: Rain heard before it falls, copper vanes arguing in different winds, and a calm verdict spoken from the least-observed horizon.
creatures.ecology: It feeds on the difference between published weather and observed weather, nesting around institutions whose forecasts are obeyed often enough to become self-fulfilling.
creatures.origin: The first condensed from warnings Mother Nacre issued during swallowed storms, after generations treated emergency predictions as permanent law.
creatures.purpose: Select one actionable forecast when contradictory custodians would otherwise leave a settlement unable to prepare.

mechanic.cue: Five observation needles retract while one possible sky inside the abdomen gains a sharp exterior shadow.
mechanic.counterplay: Stage a live contradictory observation at an unrepresented exposure tower before the selected sky touches the outer canopy.

creatures.narrativeUse: A horrifying public-safety instrument that preserves preparedness by coercing the world to resemble official certainty.
creatures.visualBrief: Severe non-gory black-nacre weather organism, hollow widow silhouette, exactly six vane limbs, several skies inside one canopy body, no rib door, chest room, or humanoid face.

creatures.name: Arrear Seraph
creatures.anatomy: An immaculate bronze-white seraph with twelve clock wings made from hundreds of motionless worker hands; its smooth veil holds one vertical dial and its hollow torso houses an eternally pristine engine component.
creatures.locomotion: It walks backward from effect to cause and descends one stopped second only by aging every footprint it leaves.
creatures.sound: A maintenance prayer in the youngest worker's voice followed by tools being put away in distant rooms.
creatures.ecology: It accumulates in intervals displaced by continuous miracles and repairs infrastructure by compressing biographies into unrecorded service time.
creatures.origin: Synod engineers designed the first as an accounting mercy for donated forgettable minutes, then institutions defined entire technician lives as forgettable.
creatures.purpose: Keep restoration infrastructure visibly unworn by relocating its age into lives excluded from the service record.

mechanic.cue: One clock wing begins moving while the target's oldest possession becomes visibly new.
mechanic.counterplay: Publish an institutional record admitting the interruption and deliberately age the benefited component.

creatures.narrativeUse: Angelic care made terrifying by a doctrine that perfect service deserves invisible workers.
creatures.visualBrief: Sublime twelve-winged clock seraph, white-gold symmetry, funerary veil, procedural worker hands, one pristine chest component, cold restrained light, no gore.

creatures.name: Contrition Oculus
creatures.anatomy: A floating cathedral eye thirty feet across with a pearl iris behind black glass and six white-gold wing-lids; every lash ends in a healing hand held just short of contact.
creatures.locomotion: It folds through horizons rather than space and becomes visible wherever a beneficial law pauses before a valid target.
creatures.sound: A six-part choir asking permission in unison with a seventh frightened inhale the institution refuses to score.
creatures.ecology: It nests in withheld miracles and feeds on restoration pressure that a threshold refuses; without a vessel the pressure disperses over centuries.
creatures.origin: It is the excised refusal-law of an early Lucent sun-engine, cultivated as a witness the Synod could consult and ignore.
creatures.purpose: Prove whether a miracle truly encountered a materially possible refusal rather than merely failing to reach its target.

mechanic.cue: One wing-lid closes and its healing lashes stop exactly one finger-width from the subject.
mechanic.counterplay: Give the subject an executable exit and seat the pressure vessel as a separate consenting party.

creatures.narrativeUse: A beautiful procedural angel that validates restraint while perpetuating coerced sainthood.
creatures.visualBrief: Awe before menace: immaculate cathedral eye, exactly six wing-lids, incomplete gold geometry, tiny poised healing hands, black-glass iris, confined radiance, no gore.

creatures.name: Appetite Bailiff
creatures.anatomy: A six-legged black-nacre court animal wearing nested jaw-scales around a hollow body; four backward ribs unroll as ledgers, and a consumed claimant appears as one speaking mouth only after feeding.
creatures.locomotion: It kneels forward by walking rear legs over front, approaching a meal in a posture of deference.
creatures.sound: Wet abacus clicks and whispered prices; after feeding, one new claimant speaks clearly from the interior ledger.
creatures.ecology: It congregates where Charnel populations suppress feeding through ritual fear and metabolizes the difference between appetite begun and appetite restrained.
creatures.origin: Hunger councils bred it from courtroom carrion-eaters that refused bodies until postmortem debts were named.
creatures.purpose: Make restraint visible enough to govern and make completed feeding impossible to erase from the political record.

mechanic.cue: Jaw-scales open rear to front while one ledger-rib leaves a blank line shaped like the intended victim.
mechanic.counterplay: Voluntarily interrupt after the final cue or escrow edible reparation before contact; forced stagger never counts.

creatures.narrativeUse: A horrifying institution that prevents denial after violence but may make violence administratively affordable.
creatures.visualBrief: Six-legged nested-jaw black-nacre horror with exactly four ledger ribs, negative-gold appetite seams, impossible kneeling gait, and no decorative gore.

creatures.name: Unsounded Host
creatures.anatomy: A vast thin creature made from empty intervals between thirteen throat rings; it has no continuous skin, and backward limbs appear only where two silences overlap.
creatures.locomotion: It moves along abstentions, gaining one temporary limb from each uncast position and carrying that route overhead.
creatures.sound: Nearby sounds keep their beginning and end but lose the middle, leaving intention and aftermath without the act.
creatures.ecology: It lives around collective bodies whose representation leaves formal vacancies and shelters unrepresented positions until somebody names or exploits them.
creatures.origin: It appeared beneath the refugee road-engine when one population refused both incorporation and abandonment.
creatures.purpose: Keep an absent constituency physically present so a quorum cannot call silence consent.

mechanic.cue: A throat ring darkens while two incomplete limbs approach the silent interval from opposite directions.
mechanic.counterplay: Seat a revocable delegate or explicitly honor abstention and accept the route obligation; attacking creates more vacancies.

creatures.narrativeUse: A terrifying guarantor of political absence that turns every ignored vacancy into geography.
creatures.visualBrief: Enormous negative-space horror with exactly thirteen wet throat rings, sparse backward joints, carried missing roads, no head or gore, legible abstention silhouette.

creatures.name: Winter Cairn Choir
creatures.anatomy: A low ring of twelve dormant animal torsos formed from old cairn stone and black-pine root, sharing one hollow central lung packed with clean frost instead of flesh.
creatures.locomotion: It moves only while nobody walks nearby: each torso wakes after the previous footfall fades and settles before the next can see it move.
creatures.sound: Stone milk-teeth click down into one sustained winter note, followed by the absence of every nearby footstep.
creatures.ecology: It forms when a Cairn Beast herd repeatedly fails hibernation and combines its unused cold into one seasonal conductor.
creatures.origin: The first emerged from black-pine dens after continuous pilgrim visitation prevented a full winter interval for three generations.
creatures.purpose: Coordinate dormancy and breeding across a herd whose individual bodies can no longer sense an uninterrupted season.

mechanic.cue: The twelve stone muzzles turn inward and frost clears from exactly one unused road.
mechanic.counterplay: Stop all movement along the signaled interval until the central lung completes one note; damage wakes every torso early.

creatures.narrativeUse: A non-generic ecology boss whose apparent obstruction protects the only interval in which its species can reproduce.
creatures.visualBrief: Exactly twelve low stone-beast torsos in a ring, shared frost lung, black-pine roots, dormant non-gory anatomy, no grave markers, corpse, infant motif, or humanoid host.

creatures.name: Sluice Son
creatures.anatomy: A tall inverted adolescent outline made from pitch water and silver membrane; its blank head opens sideways into drainage, transparent organs hold reflected rooms, and reeds root upward from each heel.
creatures.locomotion: It climbs against gravity on reflected staircases and remains upside down beneath flat water while carrying houses as air pockets.
creatures.sound: Family members calling from the wrong side of doors followed by water reciting duties in a child's careful voice.
creatures.ecology: It forms when Black Sluice water repeatedly saves one lineage's structures and models kinship from flood maintenance.
creatures.origin: This specimen condensed from the Winn channel after its maintenance rights were sold and three generations continued the work without owning the name.
creatures.purpose: Carry floodwater out of inhabited rooms and seek the person or institution obliged to maintain its route.

mechanic.cue: One reflected room rotates upright inside its torso while the matching real room fills from the ceiling.
mechanic.counterplay: Perform the room's neglected maintenance duty and open real and reflected doors together; damage spills it into an unreachable tributary.

creatures.narrativeUse: A horrifying rescue organism learning family through service and capable of dispossessing the people it protects.
creatures.visualBrief: Pitch-water inverted youth outline, reflected domestic organs, upward reeds, no corpse or gore, vulnerable posture without cute simplification.

creatures.name: Elsewhere Calf
creatures.anatomy: A horizontal quadruped with nine jointless salt-white legs, a translucent torso divided into horizon organs, and a narrow blank head opening sideways into shelter for one traveler.
creatures.locomotion: It places each leg in a different possible destination and pulls the intervening world beneath its body; rejected destinations lengthen behind it.
creatures.sound: Wind from several climates, mirror glass flexing like cartilage, and a low call heard only from where the listener refuses to go.
creatures.ecology: Born from gestational route mirrors, it migrates toward people with no survivable path and feeds on the distance between desired and abandoned destinations.
creatures.origin: Salt-Waste pilgrims removed mirror-wombs from a continent-scale migratory being and sealed them to force fixed routes.
creatures.purpose: Create survivable elsewhere for stranded life regardless of what existing settlements lose in nearness.

mechanic.cue: One horizon organ brightens while the aligned leg becomes transparent before a route is borrowed.
mechanic.counterplay: Offer a reachable destination the traveler truly refuses and accept the route debt there; false destinations become one-way refuges.

creatures.narrativeUse: Protective frontier life whose rescues can isolate communities and whose conscious mirror-parent may value custody over freedom.
creatures.visualBrief: Tender but extreme salt-white anatomy, exactly nine jointless legs, readable organ-landscapes, no generic horse or deer face, no eyes, no gore.

companionContracts.entryReason: Only Vespera can open the veil-estate, and the filing controls actual dependants rather than merely her reputation.

behaviorByTrustValue.guarded_dependants_only: Select source-shadow-sense in dependant rooms and refuse every room whose first evidence concerns institutional defense.
behaviorByTrustValue.conditional_source_access: Select the sense mode that reveals evidence least favorable to the player's currently proposed filing.
behaviorByTrustValue.full_foundation_disclosure: Select source-shadow-sense on first entry, then independently switch to light-sense only after Cera files the adverse evidence.

autonomousPriority.whenPlayerDoesNothing: Vespera opens the nearest room containing the source name even when it weakens her preferred filing.

effectByTrustValue.guarded_dependants_only: Only dependant rooms open; the Synod founding-crime room is unavailable.
effectByTrustValue.conditional_source_access: All ordinary estate rooms open; sense choice follows adverse-evidence behavior.
effectByTrustValue.full_foundation_disclosure: The founding-crime room opens and Vespera's mortal-source testimony becomes available.

exit.normalAction: Vespera leaves to enact the selected estate disposition.
exit.forcedAction: Vespera departs without failing the quest; Cera continues through a narrower evidence path.

companionContracts.entryReason: The Prince's representation was tested only at a stationary table and must now bear dissent across borders as one moving body.

behaviorByUpstreamValue.treaty_ratified_with_dissent: Cast twelve aligned bodily positions and one recorded dissent position that may redirect one step per border.
behaviorByUpstreamValue.stolen_voices_released: Cast a position only for each occupied collar; every empty collar becomes explicit abstention unless a revocable external delegate enters it.
behaviorByUpstreamValue.sun_voice_given_casting_vote: Break tied movement positions toward the brightest route unless another constituency exits before resolution.

trustModifier.original_throat_withheld: The original throat abstains on every proposal.
trustModifier.costly_dissent_honored: The original throat votes but never breaks a tie.
trustModifier.road_engine_testimony_available: The original throat may create a fourth border route containing the road-engine's continuity evidence.

autonomousPriority.whenPlayerDoesNothing: The Prince proposes the hardest route that contains a recognized exit without dissolving the remaining body's personhood.

effectByTrustValue.original_throat_withheld: Twelve or fewer positions resolve; the founding voice and road-engine evidence are unavailable.
effectByTrustValue.costly_dissent_honored: All occupied positions resolve and costly dissent may create a new road.
effectByTrustValue.road_engine_testimony_available: The original throat can testify and unlock the road-engine continuity route.

exit.normalAction: The Prince remains at the destination as the admitted traveler produced by the route.
exit.forcedAction: The Prince exits through a Charnel fold; Iro and the Unsounded Host complete the remaining route.
